findings.title: Plan never touches the finalize entry gate that short-circuits on missing session rows, so the headline incident shape stays unfixed
findings.detail:
packages/teamlead/src/bridge/plugin.ts:7501-7514 wires the land executor's `finalize` to `resolveLandSourceSession(...)` and returns `{complete:false, outcome:'partial', reason: landCloseoutReason('source_session_unavailable')}` when it resolves nothing. packages/teamlead/src/bridge/land-source-session.ts:11-41 resolves ONLY from session rows (`getWorkflowGateEntryPrOwnerExecutionId`→`getSession`, then `getSessionsByIssue`, then `getSessionByIssue`). That is exactly the incident shape the issue is about: exploration.md records FLY-2588 land@1 `da4def17` with "两库均无 session" and FLY-2413 land@1 `2cdaff27` "无 session", both stuck at held/retry=9. In that state `runResumablePostShipFinalization` is never invoked, so nothing in §2.3 (CommDB finalization), §2.4 (cleanup delivery), §3 (absent worktree) or the archive/Linear chain ever runs — the operation just re-enters exponential backoff until held.

The plan does not name `land-source-session.ts` anywhere (grep: absent), does not name `source_session_unavailable` (absent), and lists `plugin.ts` only in §4/§6 D for the lease watchdog. research.md's call path ("land executor claim → cleanup opportunity → runPostShipFinalization → …") omits this step entirely, so the gap is inherited from research. §6's checklist is therefore completable in full while the primary defect survives. The author's own evidence/design-review-log.md already flags `plugin.ts:7500-7514` as an "additional author audit while review pending" item that is NOT yet in the plan.

Required: make the plan state how per-issue closeout is entered when zero session rows survive — i.e. that finalization is keyed on the §2.1 inventory identity (run/operation/activation attribution) rather than on one resolvable `Session`, which executionId/issueIdentifier/sessionStatus `runResumablePostShipFinalization` consumes in that case, and add `land-source-session.ts` + the plugin.ts finalize gate to a §6 implementation node with its own RED test ("land operation whose issue has no session row reaches terminal closeout").
findings.failure_scenario: Implement §6 A–F exactly as written, then replay FLY-2588 (run 627d7544, land@1 da4def17, no session row in either DB). `resolveLandSourceSession` returns undefined at plugin.ts:7501, finalize returns partial/source_session_unavailable before any evidence, CommDB, worktree or archive code runs; the operation backs off 1m→2h across 8 retries and lands in held again. The §7 acceptance row "四实例 completed+archive+Done" cannot pass for two of the four replay cases.

findings.title: 5-second max evidence age is smaller than a single reused probe's own timeout
findings.detail: §2.2 mandates "全部证据最大年龄 5 秒" while reusing the existing probes: packages/teamlead/src/bridge/tmux-lookup.ts:26 sets `TMUX_TIMEOUT = 5000` for every tmux round trip (window lookup and `discoverTmuxTargetByExecutionId`), and packages/teamlead/src/bridge/generalized-launch-recovery.ts:33 runs `pgrep -f <execId>` with `{timeout: 5_000}`. A single execution's `stateSession + commSession + window + hostProcess + daemon` sweep can therefore consume ≥10s in the degraded conditions this feature exists for, so the whole-set freshness check at the mutation/archive point (§2.1 "每次 mutation 和 archive 前重读…变化丢弃证据重算") can never be satisfied and the reprobe loop ("慢 await 后重探") does not converge. The existing in-repo precedent for the same kind of gate is 30s, not 5s (StateStore.ts:41689 `ageMs > 30_000` in `validateNeedsLeadReworkQuiescenceTx`). Either justify 5s against the measured probe budget, cap each probe well below it, or raise the budget and state it per-observation rather than per-set.
findings.failure_scenario: On a loaded host (the repo's own runbook treats load 300+ as normal) a 4-execution issue takes 12s to probe. Every mutation-time freshness recheck finds the first observations older than 5s, discards and recomputes forever; the closeout never emits `gone`, falls to unknown → partial → held, i.e. the same stuck state the ticket is meant to eliminate.

findings.title: Cutting the land lease from 1h to 20s is not reconciled with the existing retry accounting, which will burn the 8-slot budget on starvation
findings.detail: §4.1 keeps `lease_expires_at` as the single deadline and sets it to lastBeat+20s (land-executor.ts:992 is 60*60_000 today — a 180x reduction). Existing code turns a lost lease into a *retryable failure*, not a benign yield: `recordStep` (land-executor.ts:405-422) throws when `recordLandOperationStep` returns `ok:false`, and StateStore.ts:73489-73493 returns `stale_land_generation` whenever `lease_expires_at <= now` even for the rightful owner and generation. `authorizeLandEffect` (land-executor.ts:398-404) produces the same reason. `classifyLandRetryReason` (land-retry-policy.ts:77-97) has no entry for it, so it defaults to `retryable`, and `nextLandRetry` consumes a slot from `RETRY_DELAYS_MS` (1m,2m,4m,8m,15m,30m,1h,2h) with the 9th → held. The plan says a starved scheduler should "输出 over-budget 失败和升级" but never says how a lease-fencing abort is classified for retry accounting, nor that `assertEffectAuthority()` failures must be excluded from the budget. Meanwhile the 30s sweep (plugin.ts:10800) can re-claim any operation whose 20s lease lapsed. Specify the classification (a distinct non-budget-consuming `lease_lost` class, or a short immediate `next_attempt_at`) and pin it with a test.
findings.failure_scenario: Bridge spends 25s inside one `Promise.all` sweep over 20 land operations. A healthy owner's heartbeat is delayed past deadline; its next `recordStep` throws `stale_land_generation`, `release` records a retryable failure and schedules `next_attempt_at` +2h. Repeat a handful of times across a busy day and a perfectly healthy land operation reaches retry=9 → held far faster than under the 1h lease, regressing the goal.

findings.title: The new issue-terminal cleanup reservation blocks all spawn/revive with no stated release, expiry, or reopen path
findings.detail: §2.1 requires a StateStore-persistent fence that makes "所有 launch/revive 入口在副作用前拒绝 terminal closeout reservation". The plan specifies when it is written but never when it is cleared. The one existing spawn-gating fence in the repo is explicit about this: StateStore.ts:25532 documents "Founder unpark/supersede — the ONLY way a tombstone stops gating spawns", and it is founder-park-scoped by design. Extending the same class of fence to every *shipped* closeout — a path that can legitimately end in `partial` or `held` (land-retry-policy.ts:124-131) — creates an issue that can never be re-dispatched, reworked, or reopened. §5's closeout_only door explicitly requires the operation to be "未被 canceled/reopened/parked", which implies reopen must remain reachable, but nothing releases the fence to make it so. State the release conditions (operation completed, operation held/aborted, supersede, reopen, and an expiry) and add them to the §6 A checklist.
findings.failure_scenario: A shipped issue's closeout exhausts the retry budget and goes held. The terminal cleanup reservation stays on the issue. Every subsequent dispatch, revive, and rework spawn for that issue is refused at the launch entry with no documented operator action to clear it; the issue is permanently un-runnable until someone hand-edits StateStore.

findings.title: New StateStore and CommDB tables require FLY-2006 retention classification fragments that no implementation node lists
findings.detail: §2.3 adds `closeout_execution_evidence` (StateStore) and `closeout_finalization_receipt` (CommDB). scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-registry.mjs:55-62 `assertNoUnclassifiedSchema` throws `schema_unclassified:<db>:<table>` for any table with no registry entry, and it is enforced from packages/teamlead/src/__tests__/fly-2006-database-retention-sweep.test.ts, fly-2413-retention-registry.test.ts, fly-2563-retention-protection.test.ts and bridge/__tests__/customer-release-store.test.ts against both the teamlead and comm schemas. The plan never mentions retention (grep: absent in plan.md and research.md) and none of the §6 A/B file lists include scripts/lib/fly-2006-retention-tables/. The §6 F acceptance command also omits every one of those suites, so the omission would only surface at CI. Add the fragments (classification per table) and the affected suites to §6 B.
findings.failure_scenario: Implementer finishes §6 A and B, the focused command in §6 F passes, the branch is pushed, and CI teamlead shards fail with `schema_unclassified:teamlead:closeout_execution_evidence` / `schema_unclassified:comm:closeout_finalization_receipt` — after the plan's own acceptance gate reported green.

findings.title: Leaf ENOENT is treated as absent without requiring the expected parent directory to exist
findings.detail: §3 says "在 repo lock 内 `lstat` 精确目标路径；仅 ENOENT 为 absent" and lists EACCES/EIO/ENOTDIR/symlink/损坏 parent as non-absent, but never requires the immediate parent to be present and to be the expected project worktree parent. `lstat` returns ENOENT identically when the leaf was removed and when an ancestor (the project's `worktrees/<project>` dir, or an unmounted volume) disappeared. The repo's own canonicalizer already anticipates the missing-path case by walking up to the first existing ancestor (packages/edge-worker/src/worktree-paths.ts:9-31), which the plan would silently inherit — so a vanished parent yields a canonical path that still "looks right" and every bound worktree under it attests absent at once. Make the plan require: resolve `dirname(boundPath)`, require it to exist and to equal `WorktreeManager.expectedWorktree(...)`'s parent for this project, and only then accept leaf ENOENT as absent.
findings.failure_scenario: The project's worktrees parent directory is renamed or its volume is not mounted. Every open issue's bound worktree lstat returns ENOENT, `cleanupState:'absent'` is produced for all of them, post-ship-finalization accepts each as cleaned and proceeds to terminal notification, thread archive and Linear Done — while the worktrees still exist under the moved parent.

findings.title: New finalizeProvenGoneSession duplicates an existing guarded API without stating the relationship
findings.detail: packages/flywheel-comm/src/db.ts:8609-8710 `finalizeSessionCommunications(executionId, expectedTmuxWindow, deleteSessionIdentity, authoritativeTerminalStatus)` already implements, inside one IMMEDIATE transaction: exact-target CAS (`target_changed`), terminal-evidence check, TURN-holder veto, effective-parked veto, unread founder-wake veto, and identity deletion gated on independent death proof — i.e. nearly the whole §2.3 contract. Its doc comment states it is exactly the "caller with independent death proof" entry point. The genuinely new requirements are the missing-row case (today `session?.tmux_window !== expectedTarget` rejects an absent row), controller generation, evidence expiry, `expired_by_closeout`, and the reservation receipt. The plan neither names this method (grep: absent) nor says whether the new one extends, wraps, or supersedes it, which is how two parked/TURN/founder-wake policies end up drifting apart in the same file. State the relationship and, in §6 B, require the existing method's own tests plus the FLY-1328 call-site sentinel to cover both entry points.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change relaxes the parked veto in `finalizeProvenGoneSession` only; `finalizeSessionCommunications` keeps the old rule. The same execution is finalized or kept depending on which caller reached it first, and the FLY-1329-shaped parked-veto regression tests still pass because they only exercise the old path.

findings.title: The §6 F acceptance command omits the regression suites that pin the exact behaviours being changed
findings.detail: All eight named paths exist and the `flywheel-teamlead` / `flywheel-comm` filters are correct (package names verified). But the command leaves out suites that directly guard the modified behaviour: src/bridge/__tests__/commdb-session-prune.fly1329-parked-veto.test.ts (the parked veto §2.3/§6 B changes), src/bridge/__tests__/post-ship-finalization.fly1434.test.ts and .fly887.test.ts, src/bridge/__tests__/close-runner.test.ts (listed as a §6 B file and in research.md's 测试落点, but absent from the command), and src/bridge/__tests__/ship-remote-branch.test.ts (a direct `getRegisteredWorktree`/attestation consumer, ship-remote-branch.test.ts:53). It also omits `pnpm --filter flywheel-teamlead test:stub-hygiene`, which .github/workflows/ci.yml:260-262 runs as a dedicated gate over post-ship-finalization.test.ts + lifecycle-routes.test.ts — the two files §6 C and §6 E both modify — under `isolate:false, fileParallelism:false` with a forced polluter-before-victim sequencer (vitest.stub-hygiene.config.ts). Since §6 F is written as the acceptance gate, a green run there can still precede a red CI.
findings.failure_scenario: Implementer runs the §6 F command, sees green, pushes. CI teamlead shard 1 fails on the FLY-1883 stub-hygiene pairing because the new lifecycle-routes/post-ship-finalization stubs leak under `isolate:false`, and the FLY-1329 parked-veto suite fails because the parked policy changed — both invisible to the plan's own gate.

findings.title: The real child-kill ≤10s wall-clock test will land in the contended parallel CI project
findings.detail: §6 D requires "真实隔离 child kill 测10秒上界并记录过程时间" as a gating assertion. packages/teamlead/vitest.shards.mjs:40-48 puts a file in the `serial` project only when packages/teamlead/ci-test-costs.json records ≥2500ms for it; a brand-new file gets `unknownFileMs` (currently 857) and therefore runs in `parallel` with `VITEST_MAX_FORKS=2` alongside other suites (scripts/teamlead-ci-shard.mjs:22-40). A real-time upper-bound assertion under fork contention is a flaky gate. Either register the new owner-liveness timing file in ci-test-costs.json so it is serial-pinned, or make the CI-gating assertion the fake-clock one and keep the wall-clock measurement as recorded-but-non-gating evidence. State whichever you choose in §6 D.
findings.failure_scenario: The ≤10s assertion measures 11.4s on a busy GitHub runner while another parallel fork saturates the CPU; CI goes red on a correct implementation, and the usual response is to widen the bound until it no longer proves the SLA in §7.
